name: DuckDB
summary: An in-process analytical database that combines embedded deployment with columnar and vectorized execution for OLAP workloads.

features.name: Embedded process execution
features.description: The database runs inside the host process without a separately managed database server.
benefits: Reduces process and network transfer overhead
costs: Database lifecycle and resource behavior are coupled to the host process

features.name: Vectorized columnar execution
features.description: Analytical queries process batches of values and use column-oriented execution to reduce per-value overhead.
benefits: Efficient scans, joins, and aggregations over analytical data
costs: The execution strategy is optimized for analytical workloads rather than every transactional workload

mathematical_views.question: How can a declarative query be transformed into composable execution operators?
assumptions: Query operators have defined input and output relations

mathematical_views.question: How does processing vectors instead of individual rows change execution cost?
assumptions: Batch processing amortizes interpretation and function-call overhead

benefits: Low operational overhead and direct host-language integration
costs: Less isolation than a separately deployed database service

benefits: High throughput for large analytical scans
costs: Workloads dominated by tiny point updates may not benefit equally

evidence.title: Why DuckDB
evidence.notes: Primary documentation for embedded operation and vectorized analytical execution.

relations.notes: Both are relational query engines with composable query execution, while DuckDB is embedded and analytical and PostgreSQL is client/server and extensible; this is a structural comparison, not historical influence or equivalence.
